dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Cryptogenic (idiopathic) drop attack — recurrent, sudden falls backward with preserved consciousness, no prodrome, and no demonstrable structural (brain and spinal cord MRI normal), metabolic, or neurological cause on bedside examination or routine blood tests, presumed to be due to a transient, self-limited failure of brainstem postural-control mechanisms.

1. Intermittent cardiac arrhythmia causing unrecognised cerebral hypoperfusion (12-lead ECG and ambulatory monitoring were not performed).
2. Orthostatic hypotension (supine and standing blood pressure were not measured; recurrent falls with leg weakness on standing in an older adult remain plausible).
3. Functional/non-organic drop attacks (patient reports inability to move all four limbs despite 5/5 power, normal tone, normal reflexes, and normal imaging — a pattern that can accompany dissociative falls).
